finding: The opt-in sparse MATERIAL preflight checked the current material references and output but did not bind those references to the imported source: clearing the material or deleting its LINE before save could silently drop a source edge.
change: Capture material-bearing entity callback handle, target, block name and LibreCAD lineage at DXF import; fail closed for missing or duplicate source identities, invalid targets, unsupported owner, incomplete capture or configured bounds.

Use one current-reference collector for source and staged checks; compare the captured references before export and on the late stability check. Retain the ordinary-save refusal and all other graph guards.
validation: Before the fix, the existing opt-in test with pre-save material clearing or LINE deletion failed 16 assertions across four source-handle and dictionary-size variants, including destination preservation checks.

After the fix, 12 focused system-codec MATERIAL cases pass 1700 assertions. Controls cover material clearing, redirection to a sibling, deletion, block rename and changed lineage, destination preservation and corrected retries. The block sample is a locally authored AC1021 DXF control.
Seven IMAGE compatibility cases pass 7512 assertions. The bundled-codec filter object compiles; this is a compile check, not a full bundled runtime test.

ezdxf reads the successful model-space AC1021 retry, finds both named materials and the intended LINE and layer references, and reports no audit errors or repairs. ezdxf also adds its own standard materials.
limits: Capture uses supported entity callbacks; it is not an independent physical scan of every entity or of absent versus explicit zero group 347.

The checks do not establish complete identity uniqueness across entities without material, all source entity types, all producer profiles, block-move semantics, native behavior or platform qualification.
Ordinary sparse MATERIAL save remains refused; this bounded opt-in test is not complete source-graph or lossless conversion proof. No generated fixture was committed.
